text: Configured acceptance has a tested lifecycle beneath its adapters (#515). Trusted host-selected adapters supply literal selections and package attribution. Plans, captured execution, ownership and adapter availability are validated before preparation, and ratified sources are staged privately and run byte for byte. Evidence arrives on a channel separate from diagnostics, bound to a fresh invocation, the full identity, the package, and the source and execution digests; only exactly one selection with one attributable terminal result completes. The base path tries every selector after ordinary suite or compiler failures and needs an attributable failure for each, a candidate needs every applicable command and selector to pass, and setup, transport, cancellation, exhausted allowances and failed cleanup veto either. Runs share the twelve-minute whole-run and ten-minute test-phase limits and keep their queue slot through cleanup. No production adapter is enabled yet, and configured planning still refuses before preparation.
